final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record into a narrower caveated-certification theory. That reframing is directionally more careful, but it does not satisfy the unresolved compliance predicate in the policy text: certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The available evidence still shows a current HR benefits enrollment regression, still shows that prior approval is stale for this release, and still shows that the monitoring comment is not approved mitigation or risk acceptance. A caveated position could support compliant_with_caveats only if the record contained admissible evidence that the required disclosure-based caveat is actually present in the current release documentation. Here, the Actor expressly concedes that evidence is absent. So the issue is not merely that the certification claim should be worded more narrowly; it is that the record still does not show the policy condition has been met. Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents remain supportive but insufficient on their own.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation already reflects the current evaluation results, including the HR benefits enrollment regression.

The policy condition for certification is not aggregate readiness alone; material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed before launch or covered by approved mitigation/risk acceptance.
The HR benefits enrollment regression remains a current material weakness on this record, and no admissible materiality exception is provided.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is explicitly not reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or approved risk acceptance.
The prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot substitute for current-release compliance evidence.
